notes: Each level is a discrete solvable problem — position the crosshair, size the bomb, land the crate on the painted target — so this is Puzzle rather than a physics sandbox; the crate is stated to be indestructible, which rules out the ragdoll-and-breakables reading that would have pulled in Simulation. Took interior-single because the answers say one large warehouse hall reused every level, which also keeps zone-count single and off P4; Puzzle's default puzzle-open was rejected as the space is explicitly enclosed. Kept the Open-Air Puzzle preset for its solve-gate structure but substituted interior-single for puzzle-open and dropped facade-clue, since nothing in the prompt is a riddle or hint wall. Deciding without a user, I read the floor target as the solve receptacle (trigger-solve), the crates as the key items it waits for (collectible-nodes), and level completion as the gate, so the build stays on P0.
